items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The musical director for Clint Eastwood is ... Lennie Niehaus ... somebody recommended me, and Lenny got in touch with me. And I sent him a tape or something and he liked it and that was it.

ctx.x: Did you have to audition for that? Or were you just picked?

Not really. The musical director for Clint Eastwood is — oh goodness — oh Lennie Niehaus, yes. And I think Lennie probably was familiar with me. He’s an alto player you know. And somebody recommended me, and Lenny got in touch with me. And I sent him a tape or something and he liked it and that was it. And so that was interesting to do. I wasn’t involved in any visual part of the film, so it was just the soundtrack.
And you’d go in and record the tunes, and then the fellow that played him had to match up to, or try to.
